entities.name: Council of the European Union
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Council of the European Union (also called the Council of Ministers or simply 'the Council') — created by the founding treaties of the European Communities in the 1950s and now one of the EU's seven formal institutions — is the body where the ministers of the 27 EU member states meet to adopt legislation, coordinate policies, and make decisions alongside the European Parliament in the EU's ordinary legislative procedure, making it one of the world's most powerful legislative bodies for a community of approximately 450 million people.

The Council of the EU operates through ten different configurations depending on the policy area: the General Affairs Council (foreign ministers coordinating EU business), the Foreign Affairs Council (foreign and defense ministers), the Economic and Financial Affairs Council (Ecofin, finance ministers), and others covering agriculture, environment, education, etc. Each configuration represents a different sector of governmental activity, and each minister in the Council represents their national government's position. Decisions are made by qualified majority voting (QMV) in most areas (55% of member states representing 65% of the EU population), though unanimity is required for sensitive areas like taxation and foreign policy.

The Council's legislative power — combined with the European Parliament in the co-decision ordinary legislative procedure — means that EU legislation adopted by the Council directly applies in or requires transposition into the national laws of 27 countries. The Council's decisions have shaped everything from EU food safety standards to financial regulation, environmental policy, and the single market's operation, affecting the daily lives of 450 million Europeans.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Council of the EU — co-adopting legislation governing 450 million Europeans alongside the Parliament — is historically significant as the primary intergovernmental institution of the world's most ambitious supranational governance experiment.
